thread:
Elena: Quick follow-up from the pricing section of today's all-hands — dropping answers + follow-ups here. Ask about quotas / credits / rate limits and we'll triage.

Raj: Can you clarify "metering buckets" behavior for bulk model migrations? We plan a large one next month and want to avoid sudden quota exhaustion.

Maya: Short answer — we will enable temporary smoothing for migrations on request (finance + product approval). That smooths daily buckets over a retention window so you don't spike and trigger hard rate limits. Ping me with the customer/org and expected token/day and we'll open the review.

Sam: Is there a config flag customers can set now or is this internal-only?

Maya: Internal for now; planning a self-serve toggle in Console + API next quarter. For immediate needs we can set it per-tenant.

Kai: How does smoothing interact with burst credits? Say a team has dev credits left and needs to burst for a migration — will smoothing consume credits faster?

Maya: Smoothing adjusts the allocation of daily quota, it doesn't auto-draw from dev credits. Burst credits are separate. If you want to draw on credits for burst, we can configure a temporary higher daily cap + charge against credit balance.

Raj: For Dedicated customers, will there be any SLA gap if we enable smoothing? We need clarity for SRE teams.

Sam: SRE note — smoothing changes allocation but not the underlying serving capacity. SLA remains the same (latency/uptime) but throughput-based guarantees need a separate capacity commit. If a Dedicated customer expects sustained higher throughput, we should do a capacity bump not just smoothing.

Elena: TL;DR: smoothing = quota shaping, not extra GPUs. For real throughput increases, coordinate with sales/infra for Dedicated capacity.

User123: Is there a public doc for rate-limit backoff recommendations? We've seen 429s during heavy replays.

Sam: Yes — we recommend exponential backoff + jitter, and limited retry budget per request. Short snippet we gave to support earlier:```python
# pseudo
for attempt in range(3):
    try:
        resp = call_api()
        break
    except RateLimitError:
        sleep((2 ** attempt) * 0.25 + random.uniform(0, 0.1))
```

Elena: We'll add a more comprehensive example to the SDK docs this week.

Kai: Clarify per-route quotas — can product routes have separate buckets (e.g., embeddings vs chat)?

Maya: Yes, we support per-route and per-model buckets today. Order of precedence: per-route -> per-model -> org default. We can also apply temporary overrides for campaigns.

Raj: Any change to credit expiry or transfer rules? A partner asked if leftover dev credits can transfer between teams.

Maya: Current policy: dev credits are org-bound, expire after 12 months, not transferable between orgs. Internal transfers between teams in the same org can be approved for enterprise customers via support. We're exploring a self-serve allocation UI.

User456: Will we expose historical bucket usage in Console so teams can forecast migrations?

Elena: Yes, that's on the product roadmap for Q2 — per-route historical burn + 7/30/90d projections with simple 'migration forecast' tooling.

billing-bot: Documentation: https://docs.redwood.ai/pricing/meters-and-quotas (internal draft) :link: 

allhands-bot: Note: if you want smoothing enabled for an upcoming migration, react with :thumbsup: and tag @Maya with expected dates + peak tokens/day.

Elena: Thanks everyone — we'll consolidate a short FAQ from this thread and link it in the all-hands notes. If you need an immediate exception, DM Maya + Raj. :thumbsup:
